precepts.text: Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them. Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.
precepts.why:
Hosea said Ephraim “shall eat unclean things in Assyria,” and Ezekiel shows it is not Ephraim alone: “And the Lord said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.”

Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes. Wherever God drove the children of Israel among the Gentiles, they would eat defiled bread there. That is the condition of the twelve tribes scattered in the lands of their captivity today, the spiritual Egypt.

precepts.text: Thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days; I have appointed thee each day for a year.
precepts.point: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.
precepts.why:
The Lord gives the same count a second time, to Ezekiel: “thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.” Each day for a year. With Numbers 14 that is two witnesses to the code: a day in prophecy is a year.

Now Daniel 9 opens up. “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people”: seventy weeks equals 490 years. “from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks”: seven weeks plus sixty-two weeks is sixty-nine weeks, 483 years. That commandment started with Cyrus, when God told the Persians to let his people go to rebuild; Israel was hindered two years, then came Darius and Artaxerxes, and the building went on under Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra and Nehemiah, with Haggai and Zechariah. “the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times”: our forefathers caught hell from the nations and built with a sword in one hand and a brick in the other.

“after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: Christ crucified, not dying for himself but for the twelve tribes of Israel. “the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Rome, in 70 AD. Then the last week: “he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”, and “for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”, the abomination in the temple Christ warned about.

The total of seventy weeks has been fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians that last week has not happened yet and belongs to a rebuilt temple today, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures and going along with whatever they say because they are white. Counted a day for a year, the way the Lord counts it, all seventy weeks are done.

precepts.text: Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.
precepts.point: Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as Deuteronomy 14 says.

precepts.why:
“Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep.” The fruit of thy body is your children: the same children panicking in front of police, the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. The fruit of thy land, thy kine and thy sheep is the food we eat: it is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us.

Ezekiel says it plainly: “Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.” Defiled bread among the Gentiles, in the lands the Most High drove us to. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us, because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet.
